tips.1: Take your photo in good light
tips.2: Look straight ahead and keep your head level
tips.3: Avoid sunglasses, hats and heavy shadows
tips.4: Use a plain background for cleaner replacement

1.q: Can I submit this photo with an application?
1.a: You can create a photo in the requested size. Check the recipient’s size, background and face requirements before submitting it.

2.a: Yes. Choose a preset or custom color. The tool separates the subject before replacing the background to preserve clothing. Use Remove background if you need to refine individual edges.

3.q: How can I get a sharper photo?
3.a: Use a clear, well-lit original and avoid cropping too tightly. Check the actual resolution shown beside the preview before printing.

4.q: Can I print the photos at home?
4.a: Yes. Choose paper size and copies under Advanced, then select Print photos. Print at actual size / 100%, with fit-to-page disabled.

2.q: Why are the edges of my photos cropped?

tips.1: Visible information in the image remains

1.a: The image is rebuilt from its pixels, removing original EXIF and metadata. Visible image content and information in the filename are not concealed.

2.a: Images are re-encoded. JPG quality and file size may change. The processed result preserves the displayed image dimensions.

ocr.subtitle: Recognize text in images, review content and export a file
ocr.heroNote:
From image to text
Less retyping!

tips.2: Use the table profile for CSV or Excel
tips.3: Always review recognized letters and numbers

1.q: Do I have to retype everything?
1.a: No. Recognition extracts text for you to review. Image quality directly affects the result.

2.q: Can I export Word or Excel?
2.a: Corresponding output options are available. CSV and Excel require the table profile and review of layout, cells and values.

3.a: Recognition runs in your browser. Recognition assets download on first use; images do not need to be uploaded for OCR.

tips.1: Use a reference with a known length

tips.3: Without a reference, distances use pixels

1.q: Can every image give real measurements?
1.a: A known reference length is needed. Camera angle and perspective can affect results; measurements use the scale you set.

2.q: Can I measure areas and count?
2.a: Yes. Area mode lets you place polygon vertices. Count mode marks and counts points.

3.a: The original image with the measurements and marks you placed drawn over it.

2.q: Can each image keep its format?
2.a: Yes. You can keep formats or convert the batch to JPG, PNG or WebP where the browser supports it.

3.q: Why is a batch downloaded as ZIP?
3.a: One image downloads directly; multiple images are bundled into ZIP with their output names.

1.q: Are redactions embedded in the output?
1.a: Yes. Black rectangles and the chosen watermark text are painted directly into the exported image pixels.

2.q: Can I add a logo image?
2.a: This tool uses text watermarks. Use Quick design for logo images and layouts.

3.q: Can I edit the mark after downloading?
3.a: Continue editing in the current tool session using the available options. Exported files have boxes and text merged into the image.

1.q: Can I convert HEX, RGB and HSL?
1.a: Yes. Enter a valid value in one field to update the other fields and preview.

2.a: EyeDropper support depends on the browser. The button appears only when supported. The standard picker and code fields remain available.

3.q: Can I copy each code type?
3.a: Each HEX, RGB and HSL field has its own copy button. Choose the code type suitable for your destination.
